_doc: Strings for the interactive widgets on localized food pages. Keep every {placeholder}. Food tokens as in en.json: {q}/{Q} subject form, {o} object form. [singular, plural] pairs follow the food's grammatical number. {d} = a duration (e.g. '4–6 days'), {m} = a number of months, {p} = pantry duration, {detail} = a translated freezing explanation, {why} = a translated 'where to store it' phrase. Celsius first.

counter.ask: It's been out on the counter for…
counter.note: Room temperature means anything above 4 °C (40 °F). On hot days above 32 °C (90 °F), the limit is 1 hour.
counter.t30: Still inside the 2-hour limit. Put it in the fridge straight away, in a shallow container so it cools quickly.
counter.t60: Fine at normal room temperature. On a hot day above 32 °C (90 °F), 1 hour is already the limit, so refrigerate it immediately.
counter.t120: Two hours is the USDA cut-off. If it was warm, or you are not sure exactly how long, throw it out.
counter.t240: Past the 2-hour limit. Bacteria may have multiplied or produced toxins that reheating will not destroy.
counter.tNight: Left out overnight, it has spent many hours in the danger zone (4–60 °C / 40–140 °F). It may look fine, but it is not safe.

pantry.ask: It's been in the pantry for…
pantry.note: Assumes a cool, dry, dark cupboard with the package tightly closed.
pantry.tFresh: Well inside the {p} pantry time, as long as it has been kept cool, dry and tightly closed.
pantry.tEdge: Near the end of the {p} pantry time. Check the smell and look before using; quality is starting to fade.
pantry.tPast: Past the {p} pantry time. Shelf-stable food usually loses quality rather than becoming unsafe: throw it out if you see mould, pests, damp clumps or an off smell.

freezer.ask: It's been in the freezer for…
freezer.note: Assumes a freezer at −18 °C (0 °F) or colder. Frozen food stays safe; these verdicts are about quality.
freezer.tFresh: At −18 °C (0 °F), it is still within the {d} quality window. Thaw it in the fridge and use it within a day or two.
freezer.tEdge: Still safe, and at the end of its best-quality window. Use it in the next few weeks; texture and flavour fade after {d}.
freezer.tPast: Food kept frozen solid stays safe indefinitely, but after {m} months expect freezer burn and dull flavour. Fine for soups, sauces and baking; trim dry grey patches.

checklist.title: Tick anything you notice
checklist.ok: Nothing ticked? Good sign. Still check how long it has been stored: the bacteria that cause food poisoning are invisible.
checklist.bad: Any of these means it has gone bad. Throw it out — don't taste it to check.

q1: {Q} is safe to eat after more than {d} in the fridge, as long as it smells fine.
{Q} are safe to eat after more than {d} in the fridge, as long as they smell fine.
quiz.a1Perishable: False. The bacteria that cause food poisoning rarely change the smell. Stick to the {d} window and throw out anything older.
quiz.a1Other: Partly true. This is not a high-risk food, so a little past {d} usually means lower quality, not danger. Check for mould and off smells first.
quiz.a2: False. Freezing pauses bacteria; it does not kill them. They become active again as the food thaws, so thaw in the fridge and cook or reheat properly.
quiz.q4: The fridge door is a good place for {o}.
quiz.a4Yes: True. The door is the warmest part of the fridge, but this food resists spoilage well enough to be stored there.
quiz.a4No: False. The door warms up every time it opens. Best place: {why}
q5Perishable: {Q} left out overnight is fine if you reheat it well.
{Q} left out overnight are fine if you reheat them well.
quiz.a5Perishable: False. Some bacteria make heat-stable toxins. Reheating kills bacteria but not those toxins, so food left out more than 2 hours should be thrown away.
q5Shelf: {Q} needs to be refrigerated to stay safe.
{Q} need to be refrigerated to stay safe.
quiz.a5Shelf: False. It is shelf-stable: {p} in a cool, dry place. Refrigerating can extend quality for some foods, but it is not needed for safety.
quiz.a5ShelfNoPantry: Not for safety, but it keeps best quality longer. Follow the storage times on this page.
